text:
A: Hiya. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah.
A: Oh good. I'm Joanne. Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, this is my last one, I think.
B: Kayleigh. Mine too.
A: I saw your lanyard in your picture. Are you in care?
B: Care home. Carer. Twelve-hour days.
A: Oh, same! Well, I'm senior care assistant, I run the day shift at a home near Huntingdon. Meds, handovers, the rota.
B: Right. So you're one of the seniors.
A: Erm, yeah. Is that a bad thing?
B: Dunno. Ours just sit in the office doing their notes while we do everything. I'm not being funny but that's what it's like.
A: No, that's rubbish, to be honest. If I'm on, I'm on the floor. I do my notes after. I keep a paper notebook as well so I'm not stuck at a computer all shift.
B: Fair enough. You'd be alright then.
A: I'd hope so. I'll be honest, though, I'm the one who has a go when people are late for handover. It drives me mad.
B: Yeah, well, sometimes it's not your fault. The parking at ours is a nightmare. You're driving round for ten minutes.
A: Oh, I know, I do get that. It's the ones on their phones all shift I can't stand.
B: Yeah, they're annoying, to be fair.
A: Do you like it, though? The actual job?
B: The residents, some of them. I've got a couple of ladies with dementia, they're lovely. One of them calls me by her sister's name every morning and I just go with it.
A: Aw. Yeah, you just go with it, don't you. My dad had dementia, actually. That's sort of why I do it.
B: Oh. Sorry.
A: No, it's alright. Six years ago now. Some days it gets you, you know. When one of them goes downhill.
B: Yeah. I had one die last year. I was close to her. I cried in my car for a week, honestly. Didn't tell no one at work.
A: Oh, bless you. No, you don't, do you. You just get on with it and then you sit in the car park.
B: Yeah. Exactly that.
A: Sorry, that's got a bit heavy. What do you do when you get in? I just have Strictly on and a cup of tea.
B: True crime, mostly. Netflix murder stuff. And Love Island.
A: Oh, I can't do the true crime. Makes me too anxious, I'm checking the locks all night.
B: It sends me to sleep, to be fair.
A: Really? You must have nerves of steel. Have you had a holiday this year?
B: Tenerife. On finance, which I'm still paying off. And I had to have two drinks at the airport.
A: Tenerife! We go every couple of years. I'm terrible flying, I check the passports about five times.
B: Do you get Heart on in the car as well? You seem like a Heart person.
A: Always! And Take That, I still love Take That.
B: My mum loves Take That.
A: Oh, thanks very much.
B: Sorry. You know what I mean, though.
A: No, you're alright. Did you get Darren earlier, the warehouse one? Lovely drawing behind him, I said he should do something with—
